rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course and produce measurements. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the 0.08 m width (x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04) and placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it. The 12 mm footprint is well under the 25 mm tape width, giving clean readings. Sensor weights are proportional to x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal is the sensor-weighted lateral position of the tape and has the right sign: a line to the left gives a positive signal, which steers left. Controller: base_speed 1.2 targets roughly the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s, without going to full throttle before the controller has been characterised. kp 2.5 gives a moderate steering response (about 875 PWM per unit of signal, with a 350 PWM scale per turn unit). ki 0 avoids integral windup on bends. kd 0.2 damps the response without amplifying sensor noise much. line_loss last_direction makes the robot keep turning toward where it last saw the line, which suits a single-sided loss at a sharp bend. Expected result: the robot completes the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. The measurements tell us whether the speed is too low to finish in time (completion_time, progress), whether kp is too high or too low (steering_oscillation, rms_error, max_error), and how often the line is lost (line_loss_events). Next step: if it oscillates, lower kp or raise kd. If it runs wide on bends, raise kp. If it fails to finish in time, raise base_speed.
